question.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y+{z}^{2}$ that passes through the point $P(1,0,1).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,0,1) & =1\cdot {0}^{2}+{1}^{2}\cdot 0+{1}^{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y+{z}^{2} & =1 \\ z & =\pm \sqrt{1-x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(1,0,1)$ is the surface $z=\pm \sqrt{1-x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y}.$
